title: Buffalo Chicken and Blue Cheese Calzones
changes_from_base: Shredded cooked chicken tossed with cayenne hot sauce, mozzarella and blue cheese replaces the spinach and ricotta, and the dough is made into four smaller calzones.
summary: Hand-held pastry parcels filled with shredded roast chicken, tangy blue cheese and spicy sauce.

ingredients.item: cooked chicken, shredded (roast chicken works well)
pizza dough, shop-bought or homemade, at room temperature

steps.title: Ready oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 245 °C with the shelf in the middle position, line the baking tray with foil and brush it with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.

steps.title: Mix filling
steps.text: Combine the shredded cooked chicken, grated mozzarella, crumbled blue cheese, cayenne pepper hot sauce and ground black pepper in a bowl.

steps.title: Roll dough
steps.text: Divide the pizza dough into 4 equal pieces and roll and stretch each on a lightly floured work surface to a 20 cm circle.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Spread a quarter of the filling over the lower half of each dough round, leaving a 2–3 cm border all around, fold the top half of the dough over to cover the filling and crimp the edges firmly to seal.

steps.title: Slash
steps.text: Cut two slits about 2–3 cm long in the top of each folded pastry to allow steam to escape during baking.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.text: Lift the sealed calzones onto the oiled foil-lined tray.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Brush all over with the remaining olive oil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for about 15 min until deep golden in colour, then leave on a wire rack for 5 min before serving.

tips: Use shop-bought roasted chicken to save time—shred it by hand so the pieces stay substantial and moist rather than becoming stringy.
The hot sauce is the bold seasoning here; taste the filling mixture before sealing and add a touch more if you prefer it spicier.
Leave the calzones on the rack briefly so the pastry underneath finishes crisping and doesn't stay soft from the foil.
storage: Best eaten hot on the day of making. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
